title: Linear-time computation is polynomial time
statement: Let $f$ be a function from binary words to binary words. If there exist a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $a$ such that, on every input of length $n$, $M$ computes $f$ within $a(n+1)$ steps, then $f$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a function from binary words to binary words
there exist a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $a$
$M$ computes $f$ within $a(n+1)$ steps for every input length $n$
replaced: If some finite machine computes a string function $f$ within time $a(n+1)$ on inputs of length $n$, for a constant $a$, then $f$ is polynomial-time computable.
